sentences.text: Staurikosaurus was a small, agile, bipedal predator that measured between 2.2 and 2.25 meters in length, stood 80 centimeters tall, and weighed 30 kilograms.
The fossil record for this animal is very incomplete, consisting mainly of the spine, legs, and a large lower jaw.
It is generally depicted with five toes on its feet and five fingers on its hands, which are traits of an unspecialized dinosaur.
Staurikosaurus is considered one of the oldest known dinosaurs, appearing alongside Herrerasaurus, Panphagia, and Eoraptor.
This species was considerably smaller than its relative Herrerasaurus, possessing a femur length of 23 centimeters compared to 47 centimeters.
The first known specimen, cataloged as MCZ 1669, was found at the Jazigo Cinco site in the Santa Maria Formation of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, by paleontologist Llewellyn Ivor Price in 1936.
The genus was formally named and described by Edwin Harris Colbert in 1970.
Available teeth suggest a carnivorous diet, as the animal hunted small to medium-sized terrestrial vertebrates including cynodonts, rhynchosaurs, and herbivorous synapsids.
These teeth were serrated, laterally compressed, and curved backward toward the throat, allowing the predator to process smaller prey by working it backwards.
The mandible suggests the presence of a sliding joint that allowed the jaw to move backwards, forwards, up, and down.
The tail was relatively long, containing more than 40 vertebrae.
Ostrom suggested that this stiffened tail served as a dynamic stabilizer to facilitate leaping and running.
The genus is classified within the clade Herrerasauridae according to the scientific consensus established since 1994.
Staurikosaurus lived approximately 225 million years ago during the late-Carnian and early-Norian stages of the Late Triassic in what is now South America.
The environment where it lived was arid to semi-arid, featuring seed ferns, ferns, cycads, and conifers.
Garcia et al. (2019) referred the holotype of Teyuwasu barberenai as a second specimen of Staurikosaurus pricei, a proposal that remains controversial.
Some researchers consider Staurikosaurus more primitive than any other dinosaur because it possesses only two sacral vertebrae.
